name: Campsite
description: A ring of company tents around a fire pit at the valley mouth, with the charter company's contract board nailed to a post by the quartermaster's tent. The first place in the valley anyone has slept in a hundred years.

name: Workbench
description: A trestle bench under a canvas awning, strewn with shavings, flint flakes and half-hafted tools.

name: Campfire
description: A cook-fire with a blackened pot on a tripod and bundles of drying herbs strung above it.

name: Camp's Edge
description: A lean-to at the northern edge of camp, facing up the valley. Beside it a flat slab of grey stone has been scrubbed clean of moss and cut with old, careful lines: Ansel Morrow's warding table.

name: Meadow
description: Open grassland running down to the valley mouth, loud with larks. Rabbits everywhere, and the odd feral hen.

name: Beck
description: A clear, stony stream running down to the river, with flint in its bed and cress along its banks.

name: Gorse Scrub
description: Spiny yellow gorse and brambles, dry underfoot and buzzing with bees. Watch where you put your hands.

name: Old Field
description: A field gone back to wild flax and wheat inside the line of its old boundary. Somebody ploughed it once, and the crop never quite forgot.

name: Field Wall
description: The tumbled line of an old dry-stone wall, grown over with moss. Adders sun themselves on the warm stones.

name: Tree Line
description: Scattered birch and thorn where the meadow gives out, with dead wood lying where it fell. Easier than cutting green timber.

name: Flint Beck
description: A bend in the beck a short walk from camp, where the water runs over a bed of grey flint. Hobb sends everyone here first.

name: Lane's End
description: An old cart lane runs north between two field walls and stops dead at the Southwood's edge, as if the trees had been told to stand there. A little way in, pale mushrooms grow in a line.

name: Birch Stand
description: Pale birches crowded close where a field used to be, their bark peeling in white strips. The ground underneath is soft with a hundred years of leaves.

name: Oak Wood
description: Old oaks, broad and slow, with the ground under them turned over by boar. Some were pollarded by farmers once and have grown out into strange, many-armed shapes.

name: Clearing
description: A gap in the canopy where the sun gets in, bright with self-heal and long grass. Crows gather in the dead tree at its edge and argue.

name: Deer Track
description: A narrow path worn by deer through the bracken, with old bones where the wolves have eaten. The deer come for the salt licks, and the wolves come for the deer.

name: Damp Hollow
description: A mossy dip where a spring seeps out under the roots. Brown mushrooms grow here in fairy rings, the ordinary kind, the way mushrooms ought to grow.

name: Tumbled Farmstead
description: The footings of a farmhouse under the trees, a well with its cap stone still on, and a cellar hole full of leaves. Nobody took the stones away when they left.

name: Hunter's Lodge
description: Jory Flint's lodge in a clearing, built from a fallen farmhouse's beams, still pegged together. Pelts dry on a rack by the door; inside, a worktable stands near the ever-burning fire.

name: Far Stile
description: A stone stile in an old wall at the northern edge of the Southwood, where a field path once crossed up the valley. Nothing sings here, and the crows keep away.

name: Sunken Farm
description: A farmhouse sunk in leaf mould to its window sills, and a cellar under it that's pitch black at noon. The crocks on its shelves are still full of salt.

name: Hill Pasture
description: Short, sheep-bitten turf on the lower slopes, though there have been no sheep for a hundred years. The wind never quite stops, and the walls of old folds run up the hill.

name: Scree
description: A slope of loose grey stone that slides under your boots. Water runs somewhere underneath it, and things live in the damp.

name: Cliff Foot
description: The foot of a grey crag streaked white under the ledges where bats roost. Old yews grow out of the cracks, twisted and hard as iron.

name: Quarry Face
description: A face of soft grey stone cut back in neat steps, the chisel marks still sharp. Somebody took a great deal of stone out of here, carefully, and left the spoil in tidy heaps.

name: Ore Outcrop
description: Bare rock breaking through the turf, stained green where there's copper and speckled dark where there's tin. A bone pick will scratch it out.

name: Old Mine Mouth
description: An adit cut dead square into the hillside, with a carved lintel and a spoil heap grown over with grass. Cold air breathes out of it. Daylight reaches a few yards in.

name: Mine Forge
description: Bett Oakes' forge in the old ore-house at the mouth of the Warden mine, squared stone under a new roof of company canvas. A workbench stands clear of the bellows and charcoal clamp, and the doorway into the hill behind has lines cut over its lintel.

name: Old Mine Gallery
description: A square-cut gallery deep in the hill, pitch black past the first turning. Rotten props, old ladders, rich green seams in the walls, and over every doorway the same careful lines as the stone at Camp's Edge.

name: Lined Gallery
description: The deepest gallery ends at a wall of grey-green stone cut back in numbered blocks, with lines carved around every gap. Below it, a rust-red vein runs down into the rock, too hard for bronze.

name: Tally Cairn
description: A tall cairn on the high end of the Scarp, looking up the valley to where the Bloom begins. A slab set in its side is cut with twelve strokes, and past it you can make out standing stones in a ring across the valley.

name: Fen
description: Knee-deep water between hummocks of moss, cold enough to ache. At dusk the moss seems to rise and settle, slow as breathing.

name: Reedbed
description: Reeds over your head, rattling in the wind, with channels of black water between them. Something heavy moves in the channels.

name: Lake Shore
description: A strip of pale sand along the mere, the only dry footing for a mile. Old stakes of a fish weir stand out of the shallows.

name: Peat Cuttings
description: Old peat banks cut in steps, black and wet, with bricks of peat stacked to dry. Somebody cut these long before the company came.

name: Clay Bank
description: A slumped bank of blue-grey clay where a stream cuts into the fen. You dig it standing in the water.

name: Mere
description: Wide, still water, grey under a grey sky, cold to the thigh a long way out. Herons stand in the shallows and don't move when you do.

name: The Kiln
description: A beehive kiln of turf and clay on a rise above the fen, peat smoke curling out of it. Col Reeve's hut has a wheel and workbench under its reed roof, with a cooking fire beside it.

name: Tanning Rack
description: Pits of brown peat water sunk beside the kiln, with hides soaking in them, a rack of drying gut above, and a cutting bench nearby. It smells of the fen, only more so.

name: Heron Carr
description: A drowned wood of alder and willow where the herons nest. The nests are empty. One heron still stands among the roots, and the growth on it catches the light.

name: Old Causeway
description: A raised road of fitted stone running north across the fen, dry-footed above the water. A boundary stone stands where it meets the far bank.

name: Feral Field
description: Walled fields gone back to the wild: flax and wheat seeded from a hundred harvests nobody took in, thistles to the shoulder and mugwort along the walls. On still days a faint haze hangs over the grass.

name: Overgrown Lane
description: A sunken lane between hedges grown into a tunnel, the ruts still there under the leaf mould. Wool hangs in tufts on every thorn, and the dogs use it as a road.

name: Abandoned Steading
description: A farmhouse and byre with the roofs fallen in and the hearth still in place. Bees have the walls, and the kitchen garden has run to comfrey and nettles.

name: Threaded Hedgerow
description: An old laid hedge, thick with blackthorn and mugwort. Fine white threads run along the undersides of the branches, as straight as a warp on a loom.

name: Ward Ditch
description: A ditch and bank cut dead straight across the fields along the line of the ring, with the next wardstone standing up out of the haze to the north. Hosts stand in the long grass here, facing the stones, as if waiting to be let through.

name: Warden's House
description: A small square stone house built to the Wardens' pattern, lines cut over the door and the door barred from the outside. Whoever kept it left in a hurry and never came back for their steel.

name: The Holdfast
description: A walled farm hamlet behind a gate of silvered oak, with smoke from a dozen chimneys and pans of mugwort smouldering along the wall-top. The descendants have lived behind these walls for a hundred and twenty years. The air inside is clearer, and there's always somewhere to sit.

name: Loom and Apothecary
description: A long room at the back of the holdfast with a loom at one end, a stillroom at the other, and a workbench between them, hung with drying herbs, bolts of felt and waxed masks. It smells of mugwort, wax and honey.

name: Wardstone
description: One of the twelve: a grey-green standing stone taller than a man, cut all over with the Wardens' lines, cracked here and there with white threads in the cracks. It hums under your hand. A host stands in front of it, facing north.

name: The Seventh Stone
description: Sister Edith's stone, at the head of a sunken lane: cracked up one face, with white threads laid along the crack. Behind it is a keeper's hut with the roof still on and the hearth swept.

name: Unsealed Level
description: The level below the wardstone seam, walled off by the Wardens with a line cut across the wall like a bar across a door. The mortar has gone. The walls beyond are streaked rust-red, and it is utterly dark.

name: Overgrown Wood
description: Old forest gone under the growth: every trunk sheathed in pale threads, shelves of fungus climbing the oaks, and a floor so soft with mycelium that your feet make no sound. Spores hang in the light like dust.

name: Colonised Birch Stand
description: A stand of birches with the white threads running under their bark in rows, like the veins in a leaf. Amber resin weeps from every crack and pale moths sleep in clusters on the trunks.

name: Puffball Glade
description: A clearing crowded with puffballs the size of sheep, some split and smoking. Every step raises a cloud. The crust on the stones here is thick and good, and the air is the worst in the Bloom.

name: Elk Wallow
description: A trampled hollow under big threaded oaks, churned to mud and pale with shed spores, where the colonised elk come to stand. Bark is stripped off the trunks at antler height.

name: Crusted Hollow
description: A stony hollow where the growth has set hard over every boulder in a shell of horn-coloured crust, ringing like pottery when you knock it.

name: Grown-Over Cottages
description: What's left of a row of cottages from the old valley: walls under a skin of growth, roof beams grown through and sagging, a host standing in a doorway as if it had just stepped out to look at the weather.

name: The Fourth Stone
description: A wardstone inside the growth, where the ring bends north along the Bloom's eastern edge. Pale growth has been laid into every one of its cut lines and pressed flat, like thread through a needle. A host stands with its palms against it.

name: Standing Green
description: The old valley's village green, with a well in the middle and a ring of hosts standing round it facing inward, grown together at the shoulders. The well still gives clean water, if you can get to it.

name: The Growing Pit
description: A broad pit dug into the forest floor and terraced into beds, with growth set out in rows like a kitchen garden and little channels carrying water between them. Gill keeps it, and teaches sporecraft here to anyone Gill trusts with a dibber. The spores are as thick as anywhere, and Gill doesn't mind them.

name: The Threaded Wall
description: Where the Bloom ends to the north, a wall of grey threads as high as a barn, laid over and over each other and still growing, warm to the touch. It runs right round the Heart. Only here the threads hang loose, like a curtain over a door, and part if you push. Behind it the ground comes up, and something deep inside hums a note the stones answer from all round the ring.

name: Threaded Wall
description: The Threaded Wall, barn-high and warm, grown round the Heart in layer on layer. There's no way through it here.

name: The Parting
description: Inside the wall the threads close behind you like a curtain. The ground goes soft and warm underfoot, the hum you heard outside is in your teeth, and something crouched on the first rise is already watching the door.

name: Warm Ground
description: Bare white mat as far as the next rise, warm as a sleeping animal and faintly steaming. Nothing grows on it that could be picked. Things grow out of it that walk.

name: Thread Curtains
description: Threads hang from nothing in grey sheets, swaying though there's no wind, and hum when you brush them.

name: Shell Ridges
description: Ridges of heartshell pushed up through the mat like a frozen sea, too hard to break and warm to lean on.

name: The Keepers' Camp
description: A Warden camp from the sealing: tent poles grown into white pillars, a cold hearth, a rack of stylus-points furred over. Someone is still keeping watch.

name: The Threadwell
description: A round hollow where the network comes up out of the ground in a slow pale swell, like water over a spring. The spores are thicker here than anywhere. Someone sits at the lip with their feet in it.

name: The Keystone
description: A slab of wardstone laid flat at the Threadwell's lip, cut with the first line of the ring: one long closed line with twelve spurs, each pointing at a stone. The hum comes up through it. A stylus could re-cut it clean; a dibber could open it from the inside, the way something grows.
